page: Amazon Web Services r8in.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 64-bit x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The compute configuration consists of 2 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 1 physical execution core via simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core, aligned with the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio typical of the memory-optimized family.

The r8in.large instance does not include integrated local SSD storage or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage solutions such as Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) for persistent data storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth rating of 3 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the dedicated high-frequency CPU cores coupled with substantial memory per vCPU provide solid memory density without requiring investment in larger multi-socket configurations.

Because this instance provides a high ratio of RAM relative to its compute core count, it is suited for workloads constrained primarily by memory capacity rather than parallel compute execution. Target deployments include in-memory caches, key-value datastores, medium-scale transactional databases, and backend services requiring substantial working memory per thread.
